description: A three-panel composite figure combining EBSD and TEM characterisation of the initial, as-quenched microstructure of Fe–30Mn–11Al–1.2C (wt%) low-density steel before cold rolling. (a) is a large-area EBSD inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the rolling-direction orientation: equiaxed grains rendered in a wide spread of colours according to the RD colour key inset labelled 001, 101 and 111, with black high-angle grain boundaries (≥15°) and red twin boundaries overlaid; a small dashed rectangle marks a sub-region. (b) is the matching phase map of the same area — the matrix is coloured blue, with black boundaries and red twin boundaries, plus scattered tiny white/grey particles; both maps carry a 200 μm scale bar. (c) is a TEM dark-field image in which nano-sized κ'-carbides appear as bright particles uniformly distributed through a dark matrix, with a selected-area diffraction pattern inset at top right and a 50 nm scale bar; the foil normal is stated to be [001]. Taken together, the panels establish that the starting material is essentially single-phase austenite containing a dense network of annealing twins and uniformly dispersed nano-scale κ'-carbides, with an almost random crystallographic texture.

subfigures.description: EBSD inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the as-quenched steel referenced to the rolling direction; large equiaxed grains in many distinct colours, black lines marking high-angle grain boundaries (≥15°) and red lines marking twin boundaries, with an RD IPF colour-key inset labelled 001, 101, 111 and a 200 μm scale bar. A small dashed rectangle highlights one region of interest. Colour spread is broad, consistent with little preferred orientation.

EBSD phase map over the same area; the whole field is uniformly blue (austenite), crossed by black grain boundaries and numerous straight red twin-boundary lines, with sparse tiny white/grey particles. Scale bar 200 μm. No second bulk phase region is visible.

TEM dark-field image with a 50 nm scale bar showing densely and uniformly distributed bright nano-scale particles (κ'-carbides) in a dark matrix; inset at top right is a selected-area diffraction pattern with a regular array of diffraction spots, unindexed in the figure.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an EBSD IPF map whose inset colour key is labelled with the three triangle corners 001, 101 and 111, i.e. the orientation is referenced to the rolling direction.
Panel (a) contains a 200 μm scale bar and shows equiaxed grains with no visible elongation or banding.
Both EBSD maps (a) and (b) are overlaid with two line colours: black boundaries and a large number of straight red lines.
Panel (b) is almost entirely a single blue-coloured phase with no large second-phase regions; only small isolated white/grey particles are visible.
Panel (c) shows bright nano-scale particles uniformly dispersed in a dark matrix at a 50 nm scale bar, with a diffraction-spot pattern inset at the upper right.
A dashed rectangle is drawn inside panel (a), marking a sub-region of the map (the caption does not explain its purpose).
The caption states that austenite is coloured blue and that black lines and red lines represent high angle grain boundaries (≥15°) and twin boundaries, respectively.
The caption states that panel (c) is a TEM dark-field image and selected-area diffraction pattern of κ'-carbides, with the foil normal to [001].
The citing text states that the phase constituent of the as-quenched material was estimated as austenite plus κ'-carbides, with nano-sized κ'-carbides uniformly distributed in the austenitic matrix.
The citing text attributes the κ'-carbides to spinodal decomposition during quenching, caused by high precipitate kinetics from the high Al and C content.
The citing text states that the microstructure contained a large amount of annealing twins and that the grain size including twins is ~70 μm.
The citing text states that the initial texture before cold rolling was almost random, as reflected by the inverse pole figure in Fig. 2(a).

measured_quantities: spatial scale of EBSD maps (μm, via 200 μm scale bar)
spatial scale of TEM dark-field image (nm, via 50 nm scale bar)
unreadable_items: Panel (a): individual grain orientations cannot be read from the map because no Miller indices are printed on the grains; only the colour-key corners 001/101/111 are labelled
Panel (b): the identity/composition of the scattered white-grey particles is not labelled in the figure
Panel (c) SAED inset: diffraction spots are visible but are not indexed to specific crystallographic planes in the figure
The purpose of the dashed rectangle drawn in panel (a) is not stated in the caption
